allObjections.title: Operator override creates governance bypass
allObjections.detail: The `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob in CA-13-A v2 allows operators to set GTM bar as low as 75, undermining the CEO directive for ≥95. This creates a permanent escape hatch where operators can ship at 75 indefinitely by never setting the override, making the '≥95 after first product' promise unenforceable.

allObjections.title: Capability-keyed naming loses agent traceability
allObjections.detail: CA-13-B v2's switch to `crawl-write-executor` and `orchestra-admission-executor` obscures which primary agent owns the sibling. When debugging production issues, operators won't know that `crawl-write-executor` belongs to Agent #21 without cross-referencing the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY, increasing operational complexity.

allObjections.title: Phase B prerequisite enforcement unclear
allObjections.detail: §11 Step 5 references 'Phase B pass per CA-14-A canonical' but CA-13-A v2 eliminates the Near-GTM conditional band without clarifying how partial Phase B passes (some paths skipped) affect clearance. The interaction between hard thresholds and Phase B skip-disclosure creates ambiguity about what constitutes a 'pass'.

allObjections.title: No migration path for in-flight products
allObjections.detail: Products currently in the pipeline targeting 75-89 Demo-ready have no documented migration path if their operator later sets `gtm_ready_bar_override: 95`. The proposal doesn't specify whether the override applies retroactively to already-cleared products or only to new clearances, creating versioning confusion.

allObjections.title: Operator-config knob risks inconsistency
allObjections.detail: The introduction of the `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob in §7.6 could lead to inconsistencies across products if operators set different thresholds. This could undermine the uniformity of the GTM readiness criteria and complicate governance.

allObjections.title: Elimination of Near-GTM band lacks flexibility
allObjections.detail: By eliminating the 90–94 Near-GTM conditional band, the proposal removes flexibility for products that are close to being market-ready but not quite there. This could delay the launch of products that are otherwise viable with minor adjustments.

allObjections.title: Sibling naming convention may cause confusion
allObjections.detail: Switching to capability-keyed sibling charter naming could cause confusion if the capabilities are not clearly defined or if they overlap with other agents. This might lead to misunderstandings about the roles and responsibilities of each agent.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback strategy in case the implementation of the `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob causes unintended consequences. This could lead to difficulties in reverting changes and potentially causing harm to the system.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Testing
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not outline a comprehensive testing plan to ensure the correctness and safety of the `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob. This could lead to errors or security vulnerabilities being introduced into the system.

allObjections.title: Inconsistent Authorization
allObjections.detail: The proposal introduces a new authorization mechanism for the `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob, but it is unclear how this mechanism will interact with existing authorization systems. This could lead to inconsistencies or security vulnerabilities in the authorization process.

allObjections.title: Operator override complexity
allObjections.detail: The introduction of `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` adds complexity to the system. Operators may set arbitrary values without understanding the full implications, leading to inconsistent product quality. The §7.6 score bands should remain canonical and uniform across products to ensure consistency.

allObjections.title: Lack of migration path
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear migration path for existing products that are already in the pipeline. This could lead to inconsistencies and potential failures in the clearance process for products that were initiated under the previous guidelines.

allObjections.title: Potential for misuse
allObjections.detail: The operator-configurable knob could be misused by operators to bypass the strict quality standards set by the canonical §7.6 score bands. This could lead to products being cleared for GTM that do not meet the necessary quality standards, undermining the overall integrity of the system.

allObjections.title: Operator Override Risk
allObjections.detail: The introduction of the `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob allows operators to set a higher GTM readiness bar, but this could lead to inconsistent application of the GTM readiness criteria across different products, potentially undermining the integrity of the GTM process.

allObjections.title: Complexity in Governance
allObjections.detail: The proposal adds another layer of complexity to the governance model by introducing an operator-configurable GTM bar, which may lead to confusion and difficulties in maintaining consistent governance practices across the organization.

allObjections.title: Potential for Abuse
allObjections.detail: The capability-keyed naming for sibling charters could be exploited by operators to bypass certain governance checks, especially if the naming conventions are not strictly enforced or monitored.

allObjections.title: Operator Config Knob Risk
allObjections.detail: The `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob in §7.6 introduces a risk of inconsistent GTM readiness standards across products, potentially leading to customer confusion and diluted brand perception if some products are launched with lower quality scores than others. This undermines the purpose of having a standardized GTM readiness process.

allObjections.title: Clamping Semantics
allObjections.detail: The silent clamping of out-of-bounds `gtm_ready_bar_override` values to [75, 100] in §7.6, while notifying admins, could lead to unexpected behavior and debugging challenges. Operators might assume their configured value is being used, leading to incorrect assumptions about GTM readiness.

allObjections.title: Reconciliation Paragraph Redundancy
allObjections.detail: The §19.0 reconciliation paragraph distinguishing Self-Audit 95/95 from GTM Readiness bar seems redundant, as the §10 governance-mechanisms table already covers these distinctions. This adds unnecessary complexity to the document.

allObjections.title: Sibling Naming Convention
allObjections.detail: While capability-keyed naming for sibling charters is generally better, the specific name `orchestra-admission-executor` might be too specific. It focuses on the 'admission' aspect, potentially overlooking other responsibilities the executor might have in the future.

allObjections.title: §7.6 override risk
allObjections.detail: The operator-configurable GTM bar (gtm_ready_bar_override) lacks enforcement for CEO directives. §7.6 allows operators to set thresholds below the CEO-mandated 95 without consequences, creating misalignment between executive intent and implementation. The clamping mechanism only handles numerical bounds, not policy compliance.

allObjections.title: Sibling naming ambiguity
allObjections.detail: Capability-keyed naming for executors (crawl-write-executor/orchestra-admission-executor) in §15.1 creates ambiguity. Unlike agent-specific names, these don't indicate primary association, risking confusion during incident debugging. The proposal lacks cross-referencing standards between primary agents and siblings.

allObjections.title: HARD threshold fallout
allObjections.detail: Eliminating Near-GTM conditional band ignores operational realities. Products scoring 89 (Demo-ready) but blocked from conditional clearance due to a single high finding may undergo unnecessary rebuilds. §11 Step 5 HARD fails to account for context-dependent risk tolerance.

allObjections.title: Phase B verification gap
allObjections.detail: CA-13-A-CT-4 conformance test only checks for conditional-clearance keywords but doesn't validate Phase B testing requirements. Agent #21's adversarial testing mandate (ENTRY 015) could be bypassed if implementation focuses solely on score thresholds without verifying interactive flow coverage.

allObjections.title: Override weakens global defaults
allObjections.detail: In CA-13-A v2 §7.6, `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` can raise the GTM bar per product while leaving the canonical threshold at 75. That creates a split-brain policy where the same clearance step means different things across products, environments, and operator views, increasing the chance of misconfigured launches and ambiguous audit outcomes.

allObjections.title: Silent clamp hides operator errors
allObjections.detail: The proposed `[75, 100]` clamping in CA-13-A v2 silently converts out-of-bounds values instead of rejecting them. In a governance path, silent coercion is dangerous because a mistaken `50` becomes a seemingly valid `75`, which can mask operational mistakes and make post-incident forensics harder than a hard failure would.

allObjections.title: Hard gate removes recovery path
allObjections.detail: CA-13-A v2 eliminates the 90–94 Near-GTM conditional path from §11 Step 5 entirely. That means a product that is otherwise launchable but temporarily blocked by a narrow, fixable issue cannot use a supervised conditional path, which may increase time-to-market and encourage risky workarounds outside the formal clearance flow.

allObjections.title: Sibling naming still underspecified
allObjections.detail: CA-13-B v2 switches to capability-keyed names like `crawl-write-executor` and `orchestra-admission-executor`, but the draft excerpt truncates the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY definitions and does not fully specify collision handling, lifecycle, or migration from the old keys. Without explicit compatibility rules, this risks orphaned permissions or duplicate executor entries during rollout.

allObjections.title: Config knob lacks audit trail
allObjections.detail: The `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob is operator-configurable but lacks a clear audit trail. §7.6 mentions admin notification on out-of-bounds override, but not regular logging of changes.

allObjections.title: Fallback clause ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The fallback clause for re-introducing a conditional path (§11 Step 5) requires ALL `high` findings to be Resolved. However, 'Resolved' is not clearly defined in the context of Self-Renewal cycles and post-fix score reflection.

allObjections.title: Sibling charter naming inconsistency
allObjections.detail: CA-13-B-v2 switches to capability-keyed naming for sibling charters. However, the rationale does not clearly justify why this is superior to the previous agent-short-name-keyed approach, potentially introducing naming inconsistency.

allObjections.title: gtm_ready_bar_override lacks migration
allObjections.detail: CA-13-A v2 §7.6 operator-config knob section defines product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override with bounds [75,100] but names no migration path or existing-product backfill; §11 Step 5 row update references the knob without specifying how ClearanceRecord entities created pre-v2 are reconciled.

allObjections.title: fallback clause weakens hard threshold
allObjections.detail: CA-13-A v2 Near-GTM elimination section's fallback clause still permits conditional paths if Panel re-introduces them, requiring only 'Resolved' high findings; this directly conflicts with §7.6 safety-invariants (a-e) that mandate diff-only + post-deploy regression guard without defining enforcement for the fallback.

allObjections.title: EXECUTOR_REGISTRY sibling keys incomplete
allObjections.detail: CA-13-B v2 §15.1 rows 21/26 switch to capability-keyed names (crawl-write-executor, orchestra-admission-executor) but the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY typescript snippet omits required updates to BaseAgent.guard() authorityNeeded set membership and api/agent/21/execute.js wiring already referenced in §15.1.

allObjections.title: Telemetry-only dims create shadow metrics
allObjections.detail: §10.1 dims 6-7 emit telemetry that operators will inevitably use for decisions despite being excluded from §7.6 score. This creates a shadow metric system where content_quality_finding and accessibility_finding accumulate in dashboards but have no canonical interpretation or threshold.

allObjections.title: Purpose field atomicity gap
allObjections.detail: CA-15-B-v2 adds product_purpose as optional free-form text on product_registry but provides no atomic-write guarantee. Unlike the 6 canonical blocks protected by CA-14-D-Q1, this field could be partially written or corrupted without triggering rollback.

allObjections.title: Drift tier thresholds undefined
allObjections.detail: CA-15-C-v2-Q3 mentions 20%/50% token-change thresholds in options but the proposal text never defines how PURPOSE_DRIFT_MINOR/MAJOR/CRITICAL are calculated. Without concrete thresholds, operators cannot predict when drift notifications will trigger.

allObjections.title: CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md creates circular dependency
allObjections.detail: CA-15-D-v2 delegates CEO re-sign triggers to docs/governance/CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md which doesn't exist yet. This file must list which files trigger re-sign, but editing CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md itself could require re-sign, creating an infinite regress.

allObjections.title: Admin-only opt-in complexity
allObjections.detail: The proposal introduces an admin-only opt-in mechanism for dimensions 6 and 7 in §10.1, which could complicate the configuration process and limit flexibility for operators who may need these dimensions without admin intervention.

allObjections.title: Telemetry-only findings risk
allObjections.detail: By making content_quality and accessibility findings telemetry-only, the proposal risks underemphasizing these important aspects, potentially allowing products with poor content quality or accessibility to pass audits without sufficient scrutiny.

allObjections.title: Purpose information ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The removal of the `purpose_record` block and reliance on an optional free-form `product_purpose` field could lead to inconsistencies in how purpose information is captured and used, as there is no structured schema or validation.

allObjections.title: Lack of Validation
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide sufficient validation for the `product_purpose` field, which could lead to inconsistent or misleading data. Specifically, §7.5 does not define any validation rules for this field.

allObjections.title: Inconsistent Scoring
allObjections.detail: The §7.6 score formula does not account for content quality and accessibility findings, which could result in an incomplete or inaccurate assessment of the product's quality. This is evident in the §7.6 score formula, which only considers crit, high, med, and low findings.

allObjections.title: Overreliance on Admin Opt-in
allObjections.detail: The proposal relies heavily on admin opt-in for dims 6 and 7, which may not be sufficient to ensure that these dimensions are properly considered. This is a concern because the admin opt-in mechanism is not clearly defined in §10.1.

allObjections.title: Complexity of admin-opt-in mechanism
allObjections.detail: The admin-opt-in mechanism for extending the quality dimensions in §10.1 introduces unnecessary complexity. It requires admin intervention for enabling dimensions that could be beneficial for all products. This might lead to inconsistent quality audits across different products.

allObjections.title: Lack of LLM-judged purpose-alignment check
allObjections.detail: Removing the LLM-judged purpose-alignment check from the Purpose-Driven Optimization loop exit criteria may result in optimizations that do not align with the product's purpose. This could lead to suboptimal outcomes that do not meet the intended goals of the product.

allObjections.title: Potential misuse of free-form product_purpose field
allObjections.detail: The optional free-form `product_purpose` field in the ProductSSOT may lead to inconsistent and unvalidated purpose statements. Without proper validation, this field could be misused or left empty, defeating the purpose of having a product_purpose field in the first place.

allObjections.title: Risk of false positives in drift annotation
allObjections.detail: The tiered drift annotation system may lead to false positives, especially in the major and critical tiers. This could result in unnecessary operator interventions and potential freezes on fixes, disrupting the continuous improvement process.

allObjections.title: Admin-opt-in complexity
allObjections.detail: The admin-opt-in mechanism for dimensions 6 and 7 introduces unnecessary complexity and potential for misconfiguration.

allObjections.title: Telemetry-only findings
allObjections.detail: Content quality and accessibility findings being telemetry-only may lead to these issues being overlooked by operators.

allObjections.title: Optional purpose field
allObjections.detail: The optional nature of the `product_purpose` field may result in inconsistent or missing purpose statements across products.

allObjections.title: Admin-only opt-in complexity
allObjections.detail: The admin-only opt-in for dims 6 & 7 in §10.1 adds complexity without a clear benefit. It introduces a configuration flag that needs to be managed and understood, potentially leading to confusion and inconsistent application of quality checks across products.

allObjections.title: Telemetry-only findings risk neglect
allObjections.detail: Treating content_quality and accessibility findings as telemetry-only in §7.6 risks neglecting these important aspects of product quality. If these findings don't directly impact the score, they may be deprioritized or ignored, leading to a decline in overall product quality.

allObjections.title: Optional product_purpose ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The optional free-form `product_purpose` field in `product_registry` lacks structure and validation, making it difficult to use effectively. The absence of a schema and the reliance on operator-supplied text can lead to inconsistent and unreliable purpose statements.

allObjections.title: Tiered drift annotation complexity
allObjections.detail: The tiered drift annotation (minor/major/critical) adds unnecessary complexity to the system. The distinctions between the tiers and their corresponding actions may not be clear, leading to inconsistent application and potential confusion for operators.

allObjections.title: Advisory SSOT-Conformance Gate weakness
allObjections.detail: Making the §27 SSOT-Conformance Gate advisory-only weakens its effectiveness. Without a hard blocking gate, operators may choose to ignore conformance issues, leading to a decline in the overall quality and reliability of the system.

allObjections.title: §10.1 dimension overlap
allObjections.detail: The proposed Content Quality dimension overlaps with existing UI/UX scoring criteria without clear differentiation boundaries. This creates ambiguity in §10.1 audit reports where the same visual/text issues could be counted under both dimensions, leading to inconsistent weighting and potential double-reporting.

allObjections.title: Optional purpose field risk
allObjections.detail: The free-form product_purpose field lacks validation or structured schema, making it vulnerable to misuse and misinterpretation. Without mandatory format rules or automated consistency checks, operators could enter contradictory, outdated, or overly vague purpose statements that undermine drift detection mechanisms.

allObjections.title: Drift thresholds arbitrary
allObjections.detail: The 20%/50% token-change thresholds for minor/major/critical drift annotations lack empirical justification. These arbitrary cutoffs may misclassify significant semantic changes as minor if token delta is low, or flag harmless refactors as critical drift, creating noise in governance records.

allObjections.title: Conformance scope maintenance
allObjections.detail: Maintaining CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md as the trigger for CEO re-sign introduces documentation drift risk. The file requires manual updates for every relevant CA, creating a brittle dependency where missed updates could invalidate sign-offs or allow non-conforming changes to bypass scrutiny.

allObjections.title: Telemetry-only weakens enforcement
allObjections.detail: CA-15-A-v2-Q2 moves content_quality and accessibility findings out of §7.6 entirely and into dashboard-only telemetry. That means a product can repeatedly fail copy/accessibility checks while still posting a clean readiness score, which undermines the existing score as an operator-facing risk signal.

allObjections.title: Admin-opt-in hides regressions
allObjections.detail: In CA-15-A-v2-Q3, dims 6 and 7 are off by default and admin-only, but the proposal still exposes them as quality dimensions in §10.1. This creates a split-brain audit where most products never see these checks in the acceptance path, so regressions can ship unless someone remembers to enable the knob product-by-product.

allObjections.title: Purpose field is too underspecified
allObjections.detail: CA-15-B-v2 replaces the canonical `purpose_record` with an optional free-form `product_purpose` string on `product_registry`, but provides no schema, length limit, provenance, or write-atomicity rule beyond a general note. That invites stale, contradictory, or promotional purpose text to become de facto canonical state without any structured validation or lifecycle management.

allObjections.title: Drift annotations may mask deadlocks
allObjections.detail: CA-15-C-v2-Q3 converts PURPOSE_DRIFT into minor/major/critical annotations, but the proposal does not specify a deterministic transition rule from annotation to operator disposition or freeze. In practice, major drift can accumulate across runs while still allowing the loop to continue, making the issue visible but not actionable.

allObjections.title: Scoped re-sign is gameable
allObjections.detail: CA-15-D-v2-Q2 limits CEO re-sign invalidation to files listed in `docs/governance/CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md`. Because that scope file is itself editable documentation, the system can drift into a state where consequential governance changes are made adjacent to, but not inside, the tracked scope and therefore avoid re-sign requirements.

allObjections.title: Overly Complex §10.1 Extension
allObjections.detail: The proposal extends §10.1 with two new dimensions (Content Quality and Accessibility) but introduces complexity with admin-opt-in and telemetry-only findings. This may lead to inconsistent application and confusion among operators.

allObjections.title: Lack of Validation for `product_purpose`
allObjections.detail: The optional `product_purpose` field is introduced without a strict schema or validation rules, potentially leading to inconsistent or malformed data entry.

allObjections.title: Removal of `purpose_record` Block
allObjections.detail: Removing `purpose_record` as a canonical block may reduce the system's ability to track and validate product purpose, potentially impacting Purpose-Driven Optimization.

allObjections.title: §10.1 dim extension overlap unresolved
allObjections.detail: CA-15-A v2 extends the existing §10.1 5-dim engine (UI/UX, API, Logic, Business Value, Security Posture) with optional dims 6/7 but provides no explicit conflict-resolution rule for UI/UX vs Content Quality double-counting, despite citing Slot 1 and Slot 10 objections from v1.

allObjections.title: product_purpose field lacks validation
allObjections.detail: CA-15-B v2 adds optional free-form product_purpose to product_registry without required-field rules, atomic-write enforcement, or schema validation, directly contradicting the §7.5 atomic ProductSSOT update invariant and CA-14-D-Q1 guarantees.

allObjections.title: §27 gate advisory weakens §25 rules
allObjections.detail: CA-15-D v2 converts the §27 SSOT-Conformance Gate to advisory-only telemetry via governance_record_entry, eroding the Locked Rules §25 requirement that every CA promotion must maintain strict conformance without operator bypass.

Reject — every CA promotion should invalidate prior sign-offs as v1 proposed.

allObjections.title: Unbounded recommendation generation risk
allObjections.detail: §7 item #8's minimal envelope lacks any rate limits or caps on recommendation volume. Without PA-1..PA-N invariants, agents could flood operators with thousands of low-quality recommendations per run, creating noise that obscures critical findings.

allObjections.title: Cost estimation without validation
allObjections.detail: The new cost.effort_hours_estimate field in §7 has no validation bounds or accuracy requirements. Agents could emit wildly incorrect estimates (0.1 hours for major refactors, 1000 hours for trivial changes) with no conformance test to catch this.

allObjections.title: Rollback procedure underspecified
allObjections.detail: §7's rollback.revert_procedure is a free-text string with no schema or required steps. CA16A-v2-CT-3 only warns on non-revertable accepted recs but doesn't validate that revert_procedure is actually executable or complete.

allObjections.title: Defer-window config lacks audit trail
allObjections.detail: §7 item #8 + §3 admin config allows per-product defer windows [1,365] days but has no requirement to log changes to recommendation_defer_window_days. An admin could set 365-day deferrals to effectively suppress recommendations without trace.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback mechanism in case the Redesign/Build Environment causes unintended changes to the ProductSSOT. This is a significant risk, as it could lead to data loss or corruption. The §29 Redesign/Build Environment section should include a detailed rollback plan to mitigate this risk.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Validation
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide sufficient validation rules for the proactive recommendations envelope. The minimal canonical envelope is too permissive, and the full schema deferred to engineering dispatch may not be thoroughly tested. This could lead to invalid or inconsistent data being stored in the ProductSSOT.

allObjections.title: Overly Complex Taxonomy
allObjections.detail: The 6-class Multi-Format taxonomy may be overly complex and difficult to maintain. The proposal should consider a simpler taxonomy or provide a clear justification for the need for six classes. Additionally, the proposal should include a plan for handling new or emerging formats that do not fit into the existing taxonomy.

allObjections.title: Overly Complex Deferral
allObjections.detail: The proposal defers too many critical details to engineering dispatch, such as the full schema invariants (PA-1..PA-N). This deferral could lead to inconsistencies and lack of clarity in the implementation phase. Specifically, §7 item #8 defers the full schema to engineering, which may cause misunderstandings and misalignments.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback Mechanism
allObjections.detail: The proposal introduces a `rollback` object but does not specify a concrete rollback mechanism for accepted recommendations. This could lead to situations where accepted recommendations cannot be safely reverted, causing potential disruptions. The `rollback` object in §7 item #8 should include a mandatory revert procedure.

allObjections.title: Vague Admin Gating
allObjections.detail: The wording for the Redesign/Build Environment (RB-Env) is vague regarding admin gating. It states that RB-Env is admin-gated but does not specify the exact workflow or approval process. This vagueness could lead to misinterpretations and potential security risks. The scope statement in the Redesign/Build Environment section should be more explicit.

allObjections.title: Minimal Envelope Risk
allObjections.detail: The minimal canonical envelope may not capture all necessary details for effective implementation, leading to potential gaps in the proactive recommendations system.

allObjections.title: Defer-Window Complexity
allObjections.detail: The per-product defer-window configuration adds complexity without clear benefits, potentially leading to inconsistent application of recommendations across products.

allObjections.title: Section Number Ambiguity
allObjections.detail: Deferring the section number for the Redesign/Build Environment creates ambiguity and may lead to confusion in the implementation and maintenance of the feature.

allObjections.title: Cost object underspecified
allObjections.detail: The `cost` object in the `proactive_recommendation` schema (§7) lacks concrete guidance on how `effort_hours_estimate`, `risk_tier`, and `blast_radius` should be determined, leading to inconsistent application and potential gaming of the system. The lack of clear definitions for `risk_tier` and `blast_radius` makes them subjective and open to interpretation.

allObjections.title: Rollback procedure ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The `rollback` object's `revert_procedure` field (§7) is optional and human-readable, which is insufficient for ensuring reliable reversibility.  Without a standardized, machine-executable rollback mechanism, the system relies on potentially error-prone manual processes, increasing the risk of failed rollbacks and system instability. The 'revertable' boolean alone is insufficient.

allObjections.title: Deferral window clamping risk
allObjections.detail: The per-product defer-window config (§7) clamps out-of-bounds values, but the notification via `agent.product_registry.defer_window_clamped.v1` might be missed by admins, leading to unexpected behavior.  A more prominent warning or blocking mechanism might be necessary to ensure admins are aware of the clamping.

allObjections.title: Ambiguity detection threshold
allObjections.detail: The stricter classifier in CA-16-C-Q2, with a confidence floor of 0.85, might lead to excessive `target_class_ambiguous` findings, overwhelming operators with dispute resolution tasks. The choice of 0.85 seems arbitrary and lacks empirical justification. This could lead to alert fatigue.

allObjections.title: Deferred schema risks divergence
allObjections.detail: CA-16-A v2's deferred full schema to engineering dispatch creates future compatibility risks. Without canonical PA-1..PA-N invariants in §7, engineering implementations may diverge from intent, particularly around mandatory validation rules. This violates SSOT's single-source-of-truth principle and could break conformance tests like CA16A-v2-CT-2.

allObjections.title: Rollback procedure inadequacy
allObjections.detail: The new rollback.revert_procedure field (§7 Proactive Recommendations) lacks enforcement mechanisms. Conformance test CA16A-v2-CT-3 only flags non-revertable recs without blocking acceptance. In complex deployments, manual revert steps may be insufficient for stateful changes, risking system instability when reversing implemented recommendations.

allObjections.title: Ambiguity severity inflation
allObjections.detail: CA-16-C v2's stricter classifier (§6 Multi-Format) mandates 'high' severity for target_class_ambiguous at <0.85 confidence. This could flood operators with false-positive high-severity tickets for legitimate hybrid formats like PWAs, diluting attention from genuine critical findings and violating §7.6's severity calibration principles.

allObjections.title: Defer-window governance gap
allObjections.detail: Per-product defer-window (CA-16-A-Q4) allows operators to set 365-day deferrals without admin oversight. This enables indefinite suppression of recommendations via recurrent deferrals, contravening the proactive intent. CA16A-v2-CT-5/6 only validate clamping, not governance of excessive deferral patterns.

allObjections.title: Mandatory fields still undercut optionality
allObjections.detail: In CA-16-A v2, `purpose_record_link` and `market_definition_link` are made optional, but the envelope still requires `category`, `title`, `rationale`, and `source` without defining how null/empty recommendations are represented when the system has only a weak heuristic suggestion. That creates a gap between the claimed “minimal canonical envelope” and real emission paths from §7.6 / §10.1, especially for cross-cutting suggestions that do not map cleanly to a single product or run.

allObjections.title: Rollback is advisory only
allObjections.detail: The new `rollback` object adds `revertable` and `revert_procedure`, but CA16A-v2-CT-3 explicitly says non-revertable accepted recommendations are only “flagged but not blocked.” This preserves the exact failure mode the Panel objected to in v1: operators can still accept recommendations that cannot be safely undone, with no hard gate or enforcement path in the canonical contract.

allObjections.title: Defer-window can hide urgent recs
allObjections.detail: CA-16-A-Q4 moves defer timing into a per-product knob with bounds [1,365], but the spec does not define any escalation or override behavior for high-severity recommendations that are deferred long-term. A product owner could set 365 days and effectively suppress repeated resurfacing of a critical systemic recommendation, which is a concrete governance regression compared with a uniform shorter window.

allObjections.title: RB-Env numbering deferral is incomplete
allObjections.detail: CA-16-B-Q1 defers the section number for Redesign/Build Environment, yet the same block continues to assert canonical scope, atomic-audit-write, and mandatory cross-references to CA-14 fix-safety invariants. This creates a half-canonical surface: implementers must wire behavior now, but the spec avoids the one piece that anchors documentation and review navigation, increasing divergence risk across mirrored copies and later amendments.

allObjections.title: Silent fallback removed without evidence
allObjections.detail: CA-16-C-Q2 tightens classification by emitting `target_class_ambiguous.v1` whenever confidence <0.85, but the proposal does not specify calibration data, class priors, or how to handle known ambiguous hybrids like PWA/SaaS shells beyond operator dispute resolution. That can convert previously working generic fallbacks into a high-severity alert storm, increasing manual workload without proving better classification accuracy.

allObjections.title: Unclear Impact of Cost Object
allObjections.detail: The new 'cost' object in proactive recommendations (§7 item #8) includes 'effort_hours_estimate', 'risk_tier', and 'blast_radius'. However, it's unclear how these fields will be used in practice and how they will affect the decision-making process for operators.

allObjections.title: Rollback Mechanism Ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The 'rollback' object is introduced with a 'revertable' boolean and an optional 'revert_procedure'. The proposal lacks clarity on how this will be enforced or validated, particularly for complex recommendations.

allObjections.title: Defer-Window Config Flexibility
allObjections.detail: The per-product defer-window configuration (§7 item #8 + §3 admin config) allows for a wide range of values ([1,365] days). This flexibility might lead to inconsistent practices across different products and operators.

allObjections.title: Minimal envelope omits validation
allObjections.detail: §7 item #8 defines cost.risk_tier and rollback.revertable but states full schema invariants (PA-1..PA-N) are deferred to engineering dispatch; no canonical rule enforces atomicity with ProductSSOT delta_log writes per §7.5.

allObjections.title: Stricter classifier lacks workflow
allObjections.detail: CA-16-C-v2-Q2 requires target_class_ambiguous at high severity for confidence <0.85 yet provides no operator dispute resolution path or tie-in to §6 deliberate error-state triggers or §11 ClearanceRecord steps.

allObjections.title: Per-product defer desync risk
allObjections.detail: CA-16-A-Q4 adds recommendation_defer_window_days to product_registry without mandating atomic update alongside proactive_recommendation.disposition in the same run, violating the atomic guarantee claimed in §7.5.
